chunks: Then return to the House and circumambulate it for seven rounds, and that is the Tawaf al-Nisa'. Then pray two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام, or wherever you wish in the mosque. Women have then become lawful for you, and you have completed all of your hajj except the casting of the pebbles, and you have exited from everything for which you had entered ihram.

key_terms.أَحْرَمْتَ: entered into ihram and its ritual restrictions
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: women, meaning marital relations become lawful after this rite
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the Ka'bah, around which the pilgrim performs tawaf
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of salat prayed after the tawaf
key_terms.رَمْيَ الْجِمَارِ: the ritual casting of pebbles at the jamarat
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: the tawaf after which women become permissible for the pilgrim
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the station of Ibrahim عليه السلام near which the prayer is performed

ai.seo_question: When do women become permissible after hajj, and what is Tawaf al-Nisa'?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal instruction concerning Tawaf al-Nisa' in the sequence of hajj rituals. It explains that after performing this tawaf and its two rak'ahs, marital relations become permissible, and the pilgrim is released from the restrictions of ihram apart from the remaining rite of stoning the jamarat.
